state: Hi, I hope you all had a good long weekend — mine was a little chaotic because my sister-in-law came to visit from Denver and we ended up repainting the guest room together, which is a whole story involving a paint tray that tipped over onto the carpet. Anyway, that's not why I'm messaging. About three weeks ago I noticed a small red, scaly patch on the inside of my left forearm, right below the elbow. At first I thought it was just dry skin from all the cleaning supplies we were using for the painting project, so I ignored it and kept slathering on lotion. But it hasn't gone away — if anything it's gotten bigger, maybe the size of a golf ball now, and it's started to itch quite a bit, especially at night when I'm trying to fall asleep. I tried an over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream my neighbor recommended and it helped the itching for a day or two but the patch is still there, with slightly raised, flaky edges. My mother had psoriasis for years so I'm a little worried this could be something similar, though I really have no idea. Could someone take a look and let me know if I need to come in? I can send a photo if that's easier. Thanks so much, and sorry for the long message — I tend to over-explain things.

chest feels tight and my hearts pounding fast just walking up stairs lately, also my knee still aches a bit from a fall last month but thats healing fine on its own. kinda worried about the chest thing tho

hey so writing about my mom again. shes 74 and something's been off for like a month now. every night after dinner she ends up on the couch holding her side, right under the ribs, says it feels tight and full even when she barely ate anything. she used to love fried chicken thursdays and now she wont touch it, says it makes her feel awful for hours after. couple times she woke up with a sour taste way up in her throat, like stuff coming back up, even sat up half the night once. i noticed her eyes looked kinda yellowish under the kitchen light last week, told her and she just shrugged it off. her pee has been darker too, like tea colored, she says its cuz she doesnt drink enough water but idk. shes lost weight without trying, maybe 8 pounds, pants are falling off her. no fever, no throwing up, just this dull heavy feeling after meals and the tiredness. she keeps saying its nothing but im not convinced, feels like its been getting slowly worse not better. can someone look at this and tell us if we need to bring her in or if this can wait for her regular checkup in november. shes stubborn about doctors so i had to talk her into even letting me send this message. thanks for reading all this, i know its a lot.
During my last two long runs my pulse jumped erratically and skipped for several seconds mid-stride, and afterward I feel a fluttering under my ribcage that lingers while I try to catch my breath.
theres a red patch on my forearm thats been spreading and flaking for about a week now, want someone to take a look b4 it gets worse

I wanted to flag something that's been bothering me for a couple of months now, ever since my husband pointed it out while I was getting dressed for a dinner party back in July. There's a mole on my upper back, just left of my spine, that he says looks different than it used to — the edges seem less round than the other moles I have, almost notched on one side, and the color has gone from an even brown to something with a darker, almost black patch within it. It's roughly the size of a pencil eraser, maybe a touch bigger now. I can't see it well myself in the mirror even with two mirrors angled right, which is part of why I let it go for so long. Over the last couple of weeks it's started to feel slightly itchy, and once I noticed a tiny bit of dried blood on my shirt collar, though it didn't seem to be actively bleeding when I checked. Separately, and I don't think this is related at all, I've been getting these dull tension headaches most afternoons from staring at spreadsheets all day at work — I already know that's just eye strain and posture from my desk setup, and I've been meaning to get a proper chair, so please don't worry about that part. What I really want is for someone to look at the mole and tell me whether it needs to be removed or biopsied, especially given how long it's been changing. I can come in whenever there's an opening, ideally before the end of the month. Thank you.

quick message about my dad, he's staying with us this month and I noticed the skin between his fingers and up onto his wrists has gone all cracked and flaky since we switched dish soap brands last week, and he keeps rubbing at it especially at night which is waking him up, and now theres some raised bumpy patches creeping toward his forearms too, and he says it stings when he washes dishes, sorry this is scattered I'm typing between making lunches and driving carpool, just want to know if he needs to come in or if we should just switch the soap back and wait it out.

For the past six weeks I have had an episode roughly once a week where I first see a shimmering, jagged line at the edge of my vision that spreads for about twenty minutes before fading. Once it clears, a deep pounding sensation sets in on the right side of my skull, behind the eye, and it builds over the next hour to the point where light and sound become unbearable. I have to lie down in a dark, silent room until it passes, which usually takes four to six hours. During the worst episodes I also feel nauseous and have vomited twice. Over-the-counter pain relievers do nothing once the pounding has started; they only help slightly if I take them during the shimmering phase. I have not had any injury, and my vision is normal between episodes. I sleep normally and my blood pressure, checked at a pharmacy last week, was 118 over 76. I work at a desk most days and stress levels have been average, not unusually high. I would like to be seen before this becomes more frequent, since it has gone from once a month to once a week over the past two months. Please let me know what testing or evaluation would be appropriate and how soon I can be scheduled.

Hi there, I hope the office had a smooth start to the new school year — ours has been absolute chaos, between three different bell schedules for three kids and a carpool spreadsheet I built that immediately fell apart because two of the other parents switched their work hours without telling anyone. My oldest just started middle school band and needs a specific reed size that apparently only one music store in town carries, so that's been its own saga. My middle child, Owen, who is nine, tried out for the fall soccer team last week and made it, which was exciting, though practices now overlap with his sister's dance class on Tuesdays, so we're juggling two cars most evenings. Actually, the reason I'm writing is that Owen fell off his skateboard in the driveway on Saturday, landed on his outstretched hand, and his right wrist has been swollen and visibly a little crooked-looking ever since; he winces and won't grip anything with that hand, even a fork, and it's been three days with no improvement. Aside from that he's been in decent spirits, watching a lot of the show he's obsessed with lately about dinosaurs, and eating fine despite the wrist. We also have his sister's dance recital coming up in three weeks and I'm trying to figure out logistics for that on top of everything else, plus my in-laws are visiting next weekend which always adds a layer of complexity to our schedule. Anyway, could someone take a look at Owen's wrist soon? I can bring him in whenever there's an opening, mornings work best before school pickup gets complicated.

My son Idris is seven. He started second grade two weeks ago at Lincoln Elementary. His teacher this year is Ms. Alvarez, who also taught his sister three years ago. He takes the bus now instead of me driving him, route 14, pickup at 7:40 am. He has a dentist appointment scheduled for next month, already confirmed. He also finished his fall allergy shots update last week at the allergist's office, no issues there. He has had a patch of skin on the back of his left knee that has been dry, cracked, and darker than the surrounding skin for about three weeks. It does not seem to bother him during the day but he scratches it in his sleep, and there are small scratch marks around it now. We have not changed detergent or soap recently. His younger brother does not have anything similar. Idris also started a new after-school coding class on Wednesdays, which he seems to enjoy so far. We are also switching pediatricians in November because our current one is retiring, so that transition is separate from this message. His height and weight were both at the 60th percentile at his last physical in August. He does not take any regular medications. Please let me know if the knee patch needs to be seen in person or if a photo would be enough for a first assessment. I can send one by email if that helps.
my stomach has been burning and acidic right after almost every meal for the past week, especially at night when i lay down, and tums arent helping much anymore so can someone call me back

For approximately three weeks I have experienced localized pain and reduced range of motion in my right knee joint, most pronounced when descending stairs, with mild swelling palpable along the medial aspect by evening.

okay so my daughter (she's 10) has been saying her heart feels like its skipping beats or fluttering randomly, like even just sitting on the couch watching tv, its happened like 4 times this week and she says it feels weird in her chest for a few seconds. probably nothing but wanted to ask a doctor about it lol

Reporting changes for review:
- home monitor readings have run 152 over 94 and 148 over 91 the past five mornings, versus my usual 128 over 80
- brief fluttering feeling for a few seconds, twice this week, while resting
- mild lightheadedness when rising quickly from a chair
- energy levels otherwise normal, no other new symptoms
please advise on next steps.
I have noticed intermittent chest pressure and a racing pulse during minor exertion, such as climbing one flight of stairs, over the past four days.

Training log update and a question. This week: Monday, 6 mile easy run, 9:15 pace, felt fine. Tuesday, rest day, foam rolled calves. Wednesday, track intervals, 8x400m, times ranged 84-88 seconds, recovery jogs between. Thursday, 5 mile tempo run planned but cut short. During the tempo run, at around mile 3, I developed a tight band-like pressure across my chest and my pulse felt like it jumped much higher than the pace should have caused, and I had to walk for a few minutes before it eased off. It happened again Friday during a much easier shakeout run, at a pace I normally wouldn't notice at all. Saturday was a scheduled rest day, no issues at rest. Sunday, long run, 12 miles, I kept the pace deliberately slow and had no recurrence, though I was watching for it the whole time. Shoes are a new pair of the same model I've used for two years, no changes there. Sleep has been around 7 hours a night, consistent. Nutrition has been normal marathon-block eating, nothing new introduced. I'm registered for a half marathon in five weeks and would like to keep training if possible, but the chest tightness combined with the pulse spike on Thursday and Friday is different from anything I've felt before in three years of running, and I want it checked before I continue hard efforts. Let me know what workup you'd recommend and whether I should hold off on intervals until then.

Over the last month, almost every long run past the six-mile mark has ended with a wave of intense cramping low in my belly that forces me to stop and find a bathroom immediately, sometimes twice in one run, and on those same days I've noticed more bloating and urgent, watery trips to the bathroom afterward, even with the exact pre-run breakfast I've used without issue for two years.

Getting up from a seated position now takes both arms pushing off the chair and about ten seconds before I can straighten fully. Stairs are manageable only one step at a time, always leading with the same leg, and there is an audible grinding sound with most steps down. Stiffness is worst in the first twenty minutes after waking and again after sitting through a movie, easing somewhat once I have been moving for a while. This has been building for roughly four months, without a specific injury I can point to.

So this has been happening for about two weeks and I finally have a minute to sit down and write it out properly, my daughter Wren who's six will just stop mid-sentence or mid-activity, her eyes go kind of distant and she stares at nothing for maybe five to ten seconds, sometimes her eyelids flutter a little during it, and then she just picks back up whatever she was doing like nothing happened at all and has no idea it occurred, her teacher actually mentioned the same thing happening in class twice last week during reading time, saying Wren just zones out and misses a few seconds of what's being said, and at first I thought she was just daydreaming because she's always been an imaginative kid who gets lost in her own world, but this feels different because it happens multiple times a day now, at home, in the car, at school, and it's always the same blank staring look followed by that few seconds of total unawareness, she hasn't fallen or hurt herself during any of them and afterward she's totally fine and back to her normal chatty self within seconds, no confusion or tiredness after, I've started keeping a little log on my phone with times just in case that's useful, and I really just want to know if this needs to be looked at soon or if I'm overreacting to something that's actually pretty normal for her age.

Hi there! I've been dealing with a burning feeling in my stomach and chest after meals for the past few days, worse with spicy food and coffee — any chance I could get something for it? Thanks so much!

For the past ten days I have had a persistent, deep throbbing headache concentrated behind my left eye that intensifies with any bright light and has not responded at all to ibuprofen, acetaminophen, or rest.

I've been noticing lately that fine print on menus and mail looks smudged no matter how I angle it or clean my glasses, and driving home after dark I've started seeing distinct rings around streetlights and headlights that weren't there before, which is honestly starting to worry me a little since I do most of the evening pickups for the kids, and it's been creeping up over the past couple months rather than happening all at once, sorry this is a lot, just trying to get it all in before I forget between school runs.
My grandmother keeps forgetting small things now, like where she puts her keys or what day it is, and yesterday she asked me the same question three times in one hour, very unusual for her.

heartburn keeps waking me up most nights this week, burning right up into my throat after eating late — my wrist's still sore from typing but that's old news, the nighttime burning is what i need help with.

Okay so between shuttling the kids to three different practices this week I finally have a second to type this out, my right knee has been getting progressively worse over the last three weeks of marathon training, it's this sharp pain right on the outside of the knee that hits hardest going down stairs or downhill on runs, and it's started swelling up a little by evening after longer runs, sometimes I feel like a popping or catching sensation right where the pain is worst when I bend it a certain way, I tried cutting back mileage for a week and icing after every run and it helped a tiny bit but as soon as I went back to a normal long run distance it flared right back up just as bad, I've got a half marathon in three weeks that I've been training for since spring and really don't want to bail on it if I can help it, but I also don't want to make something worse by pushing through, I've never had a knee issue before in probably ten years of running so this feels different from normal soreness, could someone take a look and maybe tell me if I need imaging or if I should just see a physical therapist first, sorry for the run-on message I'm typing this in the school pickup line.
Hi! A couple times this week when I stood up too fast from my desk, the room seemed to tilt sideways for a second and I had to grab the desk edge to steady myself — kind of unsettling, any thoughts?

I have to tell you, this has been a strange summer. My grandson visited for three weeks in July and taught me how to use a tablet, which honestly upended my whole routine, and then in August the community pool where I do my water aerobics closed early for repairs, so I've been walking laps around the block instead, which is its own adventure with my hip. Anyway, sometime around the pool closing I noticed my shins had developed these dry, scaly patches, kind of silvery looking, that have slowly spread up toward my knees over the past six weeks. They don't really hurt, but they flake constantly, especially after I towel off from a shower, and I've started finding little flakes on the bathroom floor which is embarrassing when my daughter visits. I tried the thick moisturizer my late husband used to swear by for his own skin troubles, and it helps for maybe an hour before the dryness comes right back. My cousin thinks it might just be from the drier air now that the season is changing, but this feels more stubborn than ordinary dry skin ever has for me, and the patches have a defined edge to them rather than just being generally dry all over. I'd like to have someone take a look, and I can come in any weekday morning since Tuesdays are the only day I have my grandchildren.

My son's soccer teammates apparently started calling him 'pizza face' this week, which he pretends not to care about, but the breakouts across his forehead and jawline really have gotten worse the last two months despite the drugstore face wash we've been using religiously. He's fourteen, so I assume hormones are involved, but I'd rather have an actual opinion than my own guesswork.

Hi again! I hope you all are doing well over there. Things have been busy on my end — my granddaughter Poppy came to stay for a whole week while her parents were at a conference, and we spent most of it doing puzzles and watching old movies, which was lovely even though she beat me at gin rummy every single time, little rascal. My tomato plants finally came in after a slow start this year, more than I know what to do with honestly, so I've been dropping baskets of them off with the neighbors. Book club this month picked a very long historical novel that I'm only halfway through and it's due in five days, so wish me luck with that. Oh, and my knee has been fine since the last round of physical therapy, no complaints there at all, which is nice for a change. The actual reason I'm writing, though, is that my right eye has been red, gritty feeling, and rather uncomfortable for about four days now, like there's sand in it, and it's been sensitive to the porch light in the evenings, which never used to bother me. There's also been a bit of crusty discharge when I wake up that I have to wipe away before I can open the eye properly. I assumed it would clear up on its own like it sometimes does, but it hasn't budged and if anything the redness looks worse than it did Monday. Anyway, once that's sorted I'm hoping to get back to my water aerobics class, which I've missed these last few weeks. Let me know if I should come in.

My uncle swears his vision has been 'a little blurry' for two weeks, which from him means it's been bad enough that he asked me to read the thermostat for him twice yesterday. He also mentions occasional flashes of light in the corner of his left eye. He won't book anything himself, so I'm doing it for him — can you fit him in this week?

Over the last three weeks of basketball season I've noticed something that's started to genuinely affect my game, which is saying something since I've played competitively for eleven years and know my own baseline pretty well. During the second half of nearly every game, once the gym lights and the sweat and the general fatigue set in, a small dark smudge, almost like a floating speck, drifts into the center of whatever I'm looking at, particularly when I glance up toward the scoreboard or track a pass coming from the far end of the court. It doesn't stay in one spot; it seems to drift around, and blinking hard only moves it rather than clearing it. I've also started misjudging distances I normally wouldn't think twice about, like the exact release point for a three-point shot, to the point where my coach asked if something was off with my shooting mechanics, which it isn't. There's no pain associated with any of this, and it doesn't happen at all during practices in daylight through the side windows, only under the overhead gym lighting at night games. I'd like to get this looked at before the playoffs start in a month, since it's clearly not going away on its own and seems to be happening slightly more often each week.
ok so my little brother keeps holding his tablet like an inch from his face and squinting hard at the tv from the couch now, wasnt like this a few months ago, kinda sus not gonna lie

I want to preface this by saying I've already ruled out the obvious parenting theory, which is that my eight-year-old is faking a bellyache to get out of homework — if that were the plan, it's a strange one, since it never happens in the morning before school, only in the late afternoon and evening, which is exactly when homework is already over. For the past three weeks he's been doubling over holding his midsection most days around 5 or 6pm, describing it as a squeezing feeling, and it usually eases up within an hour whether or not he eats. He's also had a couple of episodes of looser, more urgent trips to the bathroom that seem to track with the worst evenings, and he's gone from eating everything in sight to picking at his plate and specifically avoiding anything with cheese, which is new and out of character for a kid who used to request quesadillas nightly. No fever, no vomiting, energy at school seems normal according to his teacher. I've tried the usual over-the-counter kid antacid with no real effect. Given that this has held steady for three weeks rather than resolving, I don't think this is a passing bug, and I'd like an actual opinion rather than my own theories about dairy or homework avoidance.

Ever since my niece's wedding barbecue three weeks ago, where I probably had too much brisket if I'm honest, I've had this nagging burning sensation climbing up behind my breastbone most nights, and antacids barely touch it anymore.

ok this is kinda freaking me out but ever since the tournament last weekend i keep getting these pounding headaches on one side that come with actual flashes of light in my vision before they start, and bright gym lights make it so much worse, anyone else deal with this or should i just get it checked

not gonna lie my hands have been going numb and tingly randomly at my desk the past week, like pins and needles in both hands at the same time, comes and goes for no reason i can tell, kinda weird right
ok weird one but my chest keeps doing this thumping thing out of nowhere at my desk, like a few skipped beats then it evens out, happened like 3 times today, kinda freaking me out ngl
stomach cramps and diarrhea every time i eat before a race, been happening for months now, need advice

Since two months, I am noticing some strange things with my thinking. Sometimes I forget name of my grandchildren for few seconds, this never happen before. One time last week I get confused about street to my own house, only for short moment but this scare me. Also the television shows I like, now I lose the story, cannot follow who is who anymore. My husband say I should write to doctor about this.
lol ok so i've been getting this squeezing pressure in my chest along with feeling super dizzy the past two days, comes and goes, kinda scary ngl, should i come in
Hi! Random one, but this week everything I look at through my right eye seems dimmer and slightly washed out compared to my left, like there's a faint filter over it — anything I should do?

For the past several days I have experienced significant blurring in my left eye that makes it difficult to read text on my monitor, accompanied by small dark specks that drift across my field of vision whenever I look at a bright, plain background like a blank document or the sky, and the blurring seems to be getting slightly worse each day rather than improving.

Since one month, I have problem to read small letters, I must hold the newspaper very far from my face now to see clear. Also at night when I drive, the lights from other cars have big circle around them, like a halo, this make driving very uncomfortable for me. I think maybe I need new glasses but this happen quite fast, only one month.

My father insists his back is 'just a little stiff,' which in Dad-speak means he can no longer bend down to tie his own shoes without holding onto the doorframe for support, and it's been going on for about a month now. He also mentions a dull ache that runs down into his left leg when he's been standing at the counter too long. He will not admit this is a problem, so I am admitting it for him.

So this is going to sound like a lot but bear with me — ever since the school fair last Saturday, where by the way my daughter Lila won a stuffed llama at the ring toss that she now sleeps with every night, she's had these odd little spells, maybe four of them now, where the corner of her mouth and her right hand twitch for about thirty seconds and afterward she seems groggy and out of it for a few minutes before bouncing right back to normal. She's also complained of a mild stomachache the last two days, though that seems totally unrelated and she's still eating fine, so I'm honestly much more concerned about the twitching spells than the stomach thing.

not to be dramatic but i've got this angry red rash all over my inner thighs and armpits after the tournament this weekend, super itchy and kind of stings when i sweat, started right after we switched laundry detergents at the team hotel lol

So funny story, or not that funny honestly — I was at my desk on Tuesday finishing up the quarterly report when suddenly this shower of little black dots appeared across my vision in my right eye, like someone flicked pepper across my glasses, except it wasn't the glasses because it was still there when I took them off, and now two days later there's also this faint gray curtain creeping in from the side that wasn't there before.
My father's home monitor has shown systolic readings consistently above 160 for the past week, accompanied by two episodes of a fluttering sensation in the chest lasting under a minute each.

I find that my right shoulder has grown quite stiff and painful these past several weeks, particularly when reaching for items on the upper shelves, and I would be grateful for advice on the next step.

Hi! My son twisted his ankle on the trampoline yesterday, it's swollen and he won't put any weight on it — he's also got a scraped elbow from the same fall but that's just a scratch, the ankle's what worries me.

So this season has honestly been a whirlwind — we made it further in the regional volleyball tournament than we have in three years, which still feels surreal, and there was this whole thing with our team bus breaking down on the way to the semifinal that turned into an unexpected bonding experience with the girls from the rival team who ended up giving half of us a ride, which is a story for another day. Anyway, during the final match on Saturday, I came down awkwardly from a block and landed wrong on my left ankle, rolling it pretty badly. It swelled up almost immediately, about the size of a small orange by the time we got back to the hotel, and turned a deep purple color by Sunday morning. I iced it on and off all weekend and kept it elevated, but I still can't put my full weight on it without a sharp, stabbing pain along the outside edge, and going down stairs is basically impossible right now — I've been scooting down them sideways holding the rail, which my teammates find hilarious. There's also a fair amount of bruising that's spread up toward my calf. I've got a club tryout in two and a half weeks that I really don't want to miss, so I'm hoping this is something that can heal quickly with the right treatment, but I also don't want to make it worse by rushing back too soon. Could someone take a look this week and let me know what I'm dealing with?
threw my back out lifting my toddler out of the crib this morning and now i can barely stand up straight, sharp pain low on the left side, need to get seen asap

This might be a weird one to explain over message but here goes. About ten days ago, right around the time our whole department was slammed finishing the annual budget review — genuinely one of the most stressful weeks I've had at this job in the four years I've worked here — I started breaking out in these raised, itchy welts, kind of like mosquito bites but bigger, in random spots on my body. They'll show up on my forearm in the morning, be gone by lunch, and then a fresh batch will appear on my lower back or my thigh by evening. Individually each welt only sticks around for a few hours, which is honestly the strangest part, but there's always a new crop somewhere. My coworker joked it was stress hives from the budget deadline, and maybe she's onto something, because things have calmed down at work this week and the welts do seem slightly less frequent, though they haven't stopped entirely. I haven't changed soap, detergent, or started any new medications that I can think of, and I haven't eaten anything unusual. The itching is manageable during the day but gets pretty intense at night, enough that I've been sleeping poorly. I took an antihistamine from my medicine cabinet two nights ago and it seemed to help some, but the welts came right back the next morning. I'd like to figure out what's actually causing this rather than just guessing, especially since it's now been over a week. Let me know if I should come in or send photos first.

I am messaging regarding my mother, who is under my care. Approximately four weeks ago I observed a well-demarcated, slightly raised area of discoloration on her lower abdomen, roughly 4 by 6 centimeters, with a fine scale on the surface and a border noticeably more defined than the surrounding skin. The area has not changed significantly in size over the observation period but has developed a mildly darker pigmentation at the center compared to the edges. She reports intermittent discomfort best described as a low-grade stinging rather than pain, occurring mostly in the evening. There is no associated fever, no drainage, and no similar findings elsewhere on her body that I have identified during routine checks. She has not started any new topical products, detergents, or medications in the past two months that I am aware of, and her other chronic conditions have been stable per her most recent visit. Given the persistence beyond four weeks without spontaneous resolution, I would like this evaluated directly rather than continuing to monitor at home. I can provide photographs taken under consistent lighting if that would assist in triage, and I am available to bring her in on short notice given her limited mobility.

I am providing a status update on my father's overall condition ahead of his quarterly review. His blood pressure has remained stable on his current regimen, averaging 132 over 78 across home readings taken twice daily for the past month. His diabetes management continues without incident; his most recent home glucose readings have ranged from 98 to 145, consistent with prior months, and his last A1c in July was 6.9. He completed his podiatry follow-up two weeks ago with no findings of concern regarding neuropathy or skin integrity on his feet. His physical therapy for the left hip, ongoing since his fall in the spring, is proceeding well, and his therapist noted improved range of motion at the last session. Separately, over approximately the past three weeks, he has developed a pattern of upper abdominal discomfort occurring reliably within thirty to forty-five minutes after meals, described as a gnawing sensation, along with two episodes of dark, tarry-appearing stool that I observed directly during his care routine. His appetite has decreased accordingly, and he has lost approximately four pounds over this period per our home scale. He continues his daily low-dose aspirin as prescribed for cardiac prevention, unchanged from his existing regimen. His sleep schedule, medication administration times, and hydration have all remained consistent with his established routine, and I have kept his medication log up to date as always. Given the dark stool findings in particular, I believe this warrants prompt evaluation rather than waiting for the scheduled quarterly visit, and I would appreciate guidance on how soon he can be seen.

My father fell off a step stool three days ago and landed on his right hip. He has been unable to bear weight on that leg since, and the leg appears slightly shorter and turned outward compared to the other side. He is in significant pain even at rest. He needs to be evaluated as soon as possible.
